_comment: Golden (DAX query -> executeQueries rows) fixtures, hand-computed from seed_data.json. This is the DAX oracle (no live engine on macOS). Column keys follow the executeQueries JSON convention: 'Table[Column]' for columns, '[Name]' for named measure expressions. Compare order-insensitively. The arithmetic is shown in README.md.
_daxQueryCount: Hand-maintained on purpose. Three suites iterate the dax-handler queries — the Go golden test, the executeQueries API test and e2e/semantic-model — and each must know how many to expect, or a fixture that failed to load passes them all vacuously. Deriving it from the file would be circular: a deleted query would lower both sides together. Counting it here rather than in three source files means adding a query is one edit, in the file the query lives in.

queries.name: Total Units YoY Asset
queries.asset: Custom DAX (tutorial: ds.add_powerbi_dax_asset 'Total Units Ratio' via DIVIDE)
queries.dax: EVALUATE SUMMARIZECOLUMNS('Time'[FiscalYear], 'Time'[FiscalMonth], "Total Units Ratio", DIVIDE([Total Units This Year], [Total Units Last Year]))
queries.note: The FY2014/Apr ratio (1.8) is out of the tutorial's 0.8-1.5 band; this is the deliberately-failing asset that mirrors the tutorial's result.

queries.name: Operator Measure Asset
queries.asset: Power BI measures defined with infix operators ('Units Delta', 'Units Growth Pct')
queries.dax: EVALUATE SUMMARIZECOLUMNS('Time'[FiscalYear], 'Time'[FiscalMonth], "Units Delta", [Units Delta], "Units Growth Pct", [Units Growth Pct])
queries.note: The round-trip witness for issue #42: both measures live in the published model.bim and are read back by name, so the operators inside their stored expressions are exercised by the query, not by publication. 'Units Growth Pct' also nests a measure that itself uses an operator, and multiplies a DIVIDE() result.

queries.name: Inline Operator Precedence
queries.asset: Custom DAX with inline operators (no stored measure)
queries.dax: EVALUATE SUMMARIZECOLUMNS('Time'[FiscalYear], 'Time'[FiscalMonth], "Blended", [Total Units This Year] + [Total Units Last Year] * 2)
queries.note: TY + LY*2, not (TY+LY)*2 — the expected values differ under either reading, so this pins multiplicative-over-additive precedence rather than merely proving the query parses.

queries.name: Derived Label via SELECTEDVALUE
queries.asset: DAX label built from the grouped column (issue #47)
queries.note: A bare 'Time'[FiscalYear] in an extension expression is refused — real DAX refuses it too — so SELECTEDVALUE is the only way to DERIVE a label from the column being grouped by. [Month] exercises the other half: each FiscalYear holds two FiscalMonths, so there is no single value and the alternate is returned.

queries.name: Referential Integrity Violation
queries.note: Not a DAX EVALUATE — a DMV/schema rowset (DISCOVER_STORAGE_TABLES). Needs a separate schema-rowset handler, deferred past the DAX evaluator. Our model has no RI violations, so every RIVIOLATION_COUNT is 0.
